diagrams.title: Capacitor bank protection — what senses what
diagrams.cap: Banks are split into two equal stars with a CT between the neutrals: healthy → no neutral current; failed units → unbalance current → relay. A series reactor limits inrush current; a time delay before re-closing lets the bank discharge.
diagrams.qq: How are failed units detected in a double-star bank?

mcqs.q: Q1. Failed units in a double-star capacitor bank are detected by
mcqs.ans: Ans: (b) Neutral unbalance current relay Unequal stars → current in the neutral link.

mcqs.q: Q2. A series reactor with a capacitor bank is used to
mcqs.ans: Ans: (c) Limit inrush current and harmonics Detunes harmonic resonance too.

mcqs.q: Q3. Discharge resistors are connected across capacitor banks to
mcqs.ans: Ans: (c) Remove stored charge after switch-off Safety and safe re-closing.

mcqs.q: Q4. Series capacitive compensation of a long line
opts: (a) Is used only for voltage regulation at no load
(b) Reduces net X and raises power transfer
mcqs.ans: Ans: (b) Reduces net X and raises power transfer P<sub>max</sub> = V<sub>s</sub>V<sub>r</sub>/(X<sub>L</sub> − X<sub>C</sub>).
